meta.title: IAPStack — Own your purchase infrastructure
meta.description: Open-source, self-hosted in-app purchase verification and entitlement infrastructure. Built in Go. Store-agnostic. Deployable anywhere.
meta.og_description: Verify purchases across app stores and turn them into durable entitlements, on infrastructure you control.

hero.lede: The open-source control panel for in-app purchases. Verify transactions across app stores and turn them into durable entitlements, without giving up control.
hero.shot_alt_dark: IAPStack operations dashboard in dark theme: purchase route health, project counts, and 30 days of verification activity with a hovered day.
hero.shot_alt_light: IAPStack operations dashboard in light theme: purchase route health, project counts, and 30 days of verification activity with a hovered day.
hero.shot_caption: The operations dashboard ships inside the Go binary. Shown with a demo project and synthetic data.

route.title: From store evidence to delivered entitlement.
route.lede: IAPStack sits between app stores and your backend. Every purchase travels the same route, and every step is durable and observable.
route.store_body: Apple, Google and Huawei adapters receive receipts and server notifications.
route.verify_body: Evidence is checked against the authoritative store API before anything changes.
route.access_body: Transactions become store-neutral entitlements: allowed, denied or unresolved.
route.deliver_body: Your backend queries a versioned API and receives signed webhooks.

features.title: Infrastructure that gets out of your way.
features.lede: Store complexity stays at the edge. Your application gets a clean, durable model for what every customer can access.
features.chart_body: Each decision is recorded as allowed, denied or unresolved, so you can see at a glance whether the route from store to app is healthy.
features.chart_aria: Demo chart of 30 days of verification outcomes. Use the left and right arrow keys to read each day.
features.entitlement_body: Ask what a customer can access instead of interpreting receipts, renewals and store-specific states in your app.
features.lifecycle_body: Durable notifications, background reconciliation and a transactional outbox keep access in sync when events arrive late or not at all.
features.verify_body: Every entitlement is derived from evidence the store signed, never from a mutable client-side flag.
features.deploy_body: Run the compact API and worker together or scale them apart. Docker, PostgreSQL and documented cloud targets.

architecture.title: Credentials and purchase data stay with you.
architecture.lede: IAPStack owns the hard parts of purchase lifecycle management, while every secret, receipt and decision lives in your PostgreSQL.
architecture.check_verify_html: Verify at the source. Store adapters validate evidence with Apple, Google or Huawei.
architecture.check_project_html: Project durable access. Lifecycle evidence becomes store-neutral entitlements.
architecture.check_deliver_html: Deliver to your app. A versioned API and signed outbound webhooks.

quickstart.title: Up and running on your machine.
quickstart.lede: Start the complete local stack with Docker Compose. Generate local-only secrets, launch the services and check readiness.
quickstart.note_title: A few secrets. A real control panel.
quickstart.note_body_html: The full quickstart covers the environment variables for the database, encryption, admin access and metrics. Then open /dashboard/ and sign in with your admin key.
quickstart.callout_html: Prerelease software. The default branch is in active development and preview releases are not supported for production use.

sdks.title: One backend. The clients you need.
sdks.lede: Flutter is the v0.1 mobile client. Additional SDKs are implemented in the repository and continue along the release roadmap.

cta.title: Own the access layer.
cta.body: Build your purchase infrastructure on a foundation you can inspect, deploy and control.
